title: Two-Step Screening of the Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers in Thai Children with Language Delay and Typically Developing Children
publication: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
topic: Thai M-CHAT two-step screening in language-delay and TD toddlers
evidence_to_use: Thai two-step M-CHAT evidence; abstract reports high-risk language-delay children (N=109) and low-risk TD children (N=732), not N=292.
main_limitation: Tertiary-care/high-risk setting and follow-up design; not an AI/speech model.
why_included: Keeps Thai clinical screening context and shows why local validation matters.

title: Development and psychometric evaluation of a Thai Diagnostic Autism Scale for the early diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
topic: Thai Diagnostic Autism Scale psychometric validation
evidence_to_use: Thai cohort N=130. PDF reports sensitivity 100% and specificity 82.4% for TDAS against physician diagnosis.
main_limitation: Clinical scale administered by trained professionals; not automated speech/NLP.
why_included: Best Thai ASD diagnostic-scale anchor for the project.

title: Economic Evaluation of the Thai Diagnostic Autism Scale for Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis in Children Aged 1-5 Years Old
topic: Economic evaluation of TDAS in Thai children aged 1-5 years
evidence_to_use: Markov/cost-utility study showing TDAS-based screening can be economically favorable in Thai health-system assumptions.
main_limitation: Model-based economic evidence, not model-performance evidence.
why_included: Supports Thai implementation rationale, not AI accuracy.

title: Speech and Language in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders
topic: Speech and language profile in children with ASD, Thai clinical background
evidence_to_use: Thai clinical review/background on ASD speech-language difficulties and need for early speech-language support.
main_limitation: Narrative/background source; no AI model or validation metric.
why_included: Useful for SLP framing in Thai language.

title: Can Natural Speech Prosody Distinguish Autism Spectrum Disorders? A Meta-Analysis
topic: Natural speech prosody meta-analysis
evidence_to_use: Meta-analysis of natural-speech prosody studies; supports pitch, prosody, and speech-rate markers as evidence class.
main_limitation: Heterogeneous feature extraction and tasks; meta-analysis does not validate this project directly.
why_included: Strongest synthesis for acoustic/prosody rationale.

title: Vocal markers of autism: Assessing the generalizability of machine learning models
topic: Generalizability of vocal markers of autism
evidence_to_use: Shows performance can vary sharply across speech tasks/datasets; F1 ranges reported around 0.59-0.89 depending on generalization setting.
main_limitation: Generalizability stress-test rather than deployment validation.
why_included: Directly supports the project gap on external validation and task/corpus shift.

title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech Recordings: Machine Learning Model Comparison Study
topic: Crowdsourced semi-structured speech recordings
evidence_to_use: Compares ML models on mobile/crowdsourced speech; CNN around 79% was reported as best among compared models in the previous audit.
main_limitation: Noisy, short, app-recorded audio and limited control over recording conditions.
why_included: Relevant to real-world audio robustness.

title: Acoustic Features Characterization of Autism Speech for Automated Detection and Classification
topic: Acoustic feature characterization for ASD detection
evidence_to_use: Uses acoustic features and classical classifiers; PDF reports KNN achieving 96.5% accuracy, not Random Forest 88.5%.
main_limitation: Small controlled dataset; high accuracy likely not externally validated.
why_included: Useful as early acoustic-feature evidence but must be caveated.

title: Detecting Autism Spectrum Disorder from Raw Speech in Children using STFT Layered CNN Model
topic: Raw child speech with STFT-layered CNN
evidence_to_use: Introduces CASD-SC child speech corpus; each child produced 36 recordings; log-spectrogram CNN reports about 86.6% accuracy.
main_limitation: Conference paper, small/controlled corpus, no external clinical validation.
why_included: Supports raw-speech direction but not strong evidence.

title: Machine Learning-Based Early Prediction Model for Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants Using Acoustic Feature
topic: Infant acoustic-feature SVM prediction model
evidence_to_use: Prospective cohort; PDF reports 88 infants, 28 later diagnosed with ASD. Best sigmoid-kernel SVM: sensitivity 92.86%, specificity 93.33%, accuracy 93.18%.
main_limitation: Single clinical context and infant vocalization task; not CNN/Random Forest and not N=124.
why_included: Corrected acoustic early-prediction evidence.

title: Automated detection of adult autism from vowel acoustics using machine learning
topic: Adult vowel acoustics preprint
evidence_to_use: medRxiv preprint; 18 autistic adults + 18 neurotypical adults; best model discriminability about 89%.
main_limitation: Not peer reviewed, adult controlled-vowel task, very small sample, not child screening.
why_included: Use only as future/acoustic plausibility, not as core child-ASD evidence.

title: Autism Detection in Children: Integrating Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing in Narrative Analysis
topic: NLP narrative analysis in children
evidence_to_use: Narrative-transcript ML/NLP study; reported high performance around 96% in the prior matrix; sample described as 68 ASD and 52 TD.
main_limitation: Language-specific narrative transcripts and no clear cross-site external validation.
why_included: Directly supports transcript/NLP branch and transcription bottleneck.

title: Screening autism spectrum disorder in children using machine learning on speech transcripts
topic: ML on children speech transcripts
evidence_to_use: Scientific Reports paper using TalkBank transcript features; reports accuracy above 86% across datasets and strong logistic-regression/TabNet results.
main_limitation: Uses curated transcripts; age/dataset differences and TalkBank generalizability remain concerns.
why_included: One of the closest matches to asd-project speech-transcript workflow.

title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
topic: Noor Project fairness in ASD speech recognition
evidence_to_use: Frontiers in Digital Health paper on transformer transfer learning and fairness testing; reports strong mixed-gender performance but female sensitivity can drop sharply.
main_limitation: Fairness/performance varies by subgroup; transfer-learning setup depends on available corpora.
why_included: Essential support for bias/fairness gap in speech AI.

title: Reliably quantifying the severity of social symptoms in children with autism using ASDSpeech
topic: ASDSpeech severity quantification
evidence_to_use: ASDSpeech uses 99,193 vocalizations from 197 ASD children across ADOS-2 assessments; independent testing on 61 children; correlations with ADOS-2 severity reported.
main_limitation: ADOS-2 assessment context, not free home conversation; ASD-only severity estimation rather than ASD-vs-TD screening.
why_included: Strong rationale for graded severity scoring rather than binary-only output.

title: Multimodal AI for risk stratification in autism spectrum disorder: integrating voice and screening tools
topic: Multimodal voice + screening-tool risk stratification
evidence_to_use: NPJ Digital Medicine; 1242 children aged 18-48 months. Stage 1 AUROC 0.942, accuracy 0.86; Stage 2 AUROC 0.914, accuracy 0.852; agreement with ADOS-2 risk categories 79.59%.
main_limitation: Multimodal mobile/screening workflow; requires careful calibration and external validation despite strong scale.
why_included: Best recent benchmark for combining voice with screening tools.

title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
topic: AI-based medical device with indeterminate output
evidence_to_use: Double-blind, multisite prospective comparator cohort; 425 study completers; determinate-output sensitivity 98.4%, specificity 78.9%; 31.8% received determinate output.
main_limitation: Device abstains for many complex cases; output is diagnosis-support, not autonomous diagnosis.
why_included: Key safety precedent for indeterminate/uncertainty gating.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis: A Scoping Review of Face, Voice, and Text Analysis Methods
topic: Scoping review of face, voice, and text AI for ASD
evidence_to_use: Maps AI approaches across face, voice, and text analysis methods.
main_limitation: Scoping review; broad modality mix and depends on quality of included studies.
why_included: Good overview for multimodal landscape and modality limitations.

title: A Scoping Review of AI-Based Approaches for Detecting Autism Traits Using Voice and Behavioral Data
topic: Scoping review of voice and behavioral AI
evidence_to_use: Maps voice/behavioral computational phenotyping and discusses dataset/bias issues.
main_limitation: Review-level evidence; not a direct validation of a model.
why_included: Supports dataset diversity and bias gap.

title: AI-Enabled Technologies and Biomarker Analysis for the Early Identification of Autism and Related Neurodevelopmental Disorders
topic: AI-enabled technologies and biomarkers for early ASD identification
evidence_to_use: Broad review of AI/biomarkers across modalities.
main_limitation: Too broad for speech/NLP claims; use as background only.
why_included: Frames broader biomarker context without over-weighting.

title: AI-assisted early screening, diagnosis, and intervention for autism in young children
topic: AI-assisted early screening, diagnosis, and intervention in young children
evidence_to_use: Review of AI-assisted early screening/diagnosis/intervention methods for infants, toddlers, and preschoolers; useful for broad framing.
main_limitation: Broad review and not speech/NLP-specific enough to be a core project evidence source.
why_included: Provides current early-childhood AI screening overview while core claims rely on more specific speech/transcript papers.
